VP8 lossy intra-only keyframe encoder (pure Nim). Mirrors vp8.nim. Scope: still keyframes, single partition, no segments, default token probabilities (no adaptation), fixed skip probability. Valid output that our decoder (and any spec decoder) accepts; rate-distortion is RDO mode search over fully-quantized candidates, no trellis and no loop-filter awareness.

Vars

CurTokCosts = TokCosts
Per-frame token bit costs. Equals TokCosts until adaptive probs (Phase C part 2) install refined tables; RDO and trellis always read CurTokCosts so both automatically benefit. 
vp8LastNumUpdates: int
Diagnostic: number of token-prob updates in the last encode.

Lets

TokCosts = block:
  ## -log2 bit cost of every (start, plane, band, cx, token) path.
  var t: TokCostTable
  for s in 0 .. 1:
    for p in 0 ..< 4:
      for bnd in 0 ..< 8:
        for cx in 0 ..< 3:
          for tok in 0 .. 11:
            if s == 1 and tok == 11:
              continue
            var c = 0.0
            for (bit, prob) in items(TokPaths[s][p][bnd][cx][tok]):
              c += bitCost(prob, bit)
            t[s][p][bnd][cx][tok] = c
  t
TokPaths = buildTokPaths()

func bitCost(prob: uint8; bit: bool): float64 {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
-log2 cost of coding `bit` with VP8 probability `prob`. The bool

coder gives the 0-branch a range * prob/256 split, i.e. prob/256 = P(0): a 0-bit with prob=1 costs ~8 bits, with prob=255 nearly nothing. (Getting this backwards inverts every skewed token/mode cost and actively misleads RDO.)

Orthonormal DCT-II. The decoder's integer IDCT computes 8x this, and its final >>3 divides by 8, so quantizing this output directly by qstep round-trips (verified by flat-block tests).

proc flush(e: var BoolEnc) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Settle all bytes by padding zero bits through the coder (vpx stop_encode shape). 64 pads yield >= 63 renorms, draining the full 32-bit register; the decoder stops at real bits and ignores the tail. Directly dumping low would emit unsettled bytes. 
proc fwht4x4(blk: array[16, float64]): array[16, float64] {....raises: [],
    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Unnormalized 2D Walsh-Hadamard. Decoder computes WHT2D/8, so with quant step q the round-trip needs qw = fw/(8q) (see quantizeWht).

proc trellisBlk(F: array[16, float64]; qdc, qac: int16; plane, cx, first: int;
                lambdaT: float64): tuple[q: array[16, int32], hasNz: bool] {.
    ...raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
RD-optimal levels for one block: forward DP over scan positions with skip state (DCT_0 emitted or not), candidates {0, base, alt-rounding} per position plus EOB termination from skip=false. Mirrors writeCoeffs exactly (same trees, extras, EOB reachability), so the chosen levels emit verbatim. Distortion is in G units; caller scales lambda by TrellisScale.
